clue.text: Takes a roundabout way to work

definitions.text: Takes a roundabout way to work

parts.words: Takes a roundabout way to work
parts.note: the machine works by its sails going round and round, so it literally takes a circular route to do its job

explanation.surface: A commuter who always takes the long way to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill whose sails turn in the breeze does its work by rotating, a roundabout motion.

clue.text: Records Western ous-toms

parts.note: rites are customs or ceremonial practices

explanation.surface: Archives documenting the traditions of the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something is to set it down in writing, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Belief getting a small number into trouble

parts.note: NO is the short form of number

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up or disturb, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A faith that brings a minority into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into trouble' looks like a phrase, but 'into' is fodder and 'trouble' the anagram signal: NO plus INTO rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or opinion one holds, close to a belief.

clue.text: Eating out in Monaco is irresistible

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the code for Monaco

parts.note: MC is Monaco's international vehicle code

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Dining out in the glamorous principality is too tempting to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating out' suggests a restaurant, but 'out' is the anagram signal; Monaco gives its two-letter vehicle code, and 'in' wraps that code round the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic charm draws people in with a pull they cannot resist.

clue.text: Metal for the van

definitions.meaning: a heavy grey metal, chemical symbol Pb
the van, short for vanguard, is the front position

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a soft heavy metal, and the foremost position, as in being in the van.

clue.text: Counsel out of breath

indicators.note: out of signals that the answer is made out of the letters of breath, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer who has run out of puff.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the Bar is the collective body of barristers, the profession of counsel.

clue.text: This bird has ring round middle of leg

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
O is round in shape

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letter of the word leg

explanation.surface: A bird with a ring fitted round its leg, as ornithologists do.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested Old World bird with a distinctive call.

clue.text: Chaff, it's hurtful in time

parts.note: bad can mean harmful or hurtful
taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Teasing that feels harmless can turn wounding over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful teasing banter, which is what chaff means as a noun.

clue.text: Submitted for what the building contractor did?

definitions.meaning: handed in or presented, as a bill or report is
a builder coats a wall with render, a layer of plaster or cement

explanation.definitionFit: A rendered account is one submitted; a wall rendered has been coated with a cement finish.

clue.text: With difficulty, altering the whole arrangement

indicators.note: the letters come out only with some struggle, a sign they are being rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing the overall arrangement proves hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' may be a second anagram signal here; ALTERING rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun an integral is a whole made up of parts, a complete entity.

clue.text: Inflexible old deity in the eye of the storm

indicators.note: in joins the god and the central letter, one inside the other

parts.note: Woden is the old Anglo-Saxon chief god

indicators.note: the eye of a storm is its centre, so take the middle letter of storm

explanation.surface: An ancient god sits unmoved in the calm centre of a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the eye of the storm' gives O, the middle letter of STORM, which sits inside WODEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden describes someone stiff and lacking flexibility, as in a wooden performance.

clue.text: Be delighted about the girl

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
Joice is a girl's name, a form of Joyce

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy, being delighted.

clue.text: Took part in a running match

definitions.text: Took part in a running match

parts.words: Took part in a running match
parts.note: a match here is a marriage, and running off to make one is a secret wedding dash

explanation.surface: An athlete competing in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who elope run away together to marry in secret.

clue.text: Retreat, having only a small quantity to give away

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
an ounce is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A recluse with so little to offer that it is hard to be generous.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to inform against them, to betray or give them away.

clue.text: Thirty seconds are time enough to reach the tower

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and half the word minute is its first three letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Half a minute is all you need to get to the tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty seconds' is half a minute, so take half of MINUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque.

clue.text: Can it be after five or later, he calls?

indicators.note: after places the question that follows behind the numeral
later puts the word or at the end, after the rest

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
is it is the question can it be, asked in other words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a caller will arrive after five or later.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is a caller, someone who pays a call.

clue.text: illness must be socially acceptable in time

indicators.note: in places the letter for socially acceptable inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Being ill must be tolerated by society in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, socially acceptable, is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits, such as malaria.

clue.text: Don't put into harbour you need this document

parts.note: to pass a place is to go by without stopping or putting in
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A sailor advised to sail by the harbour finds they need papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official travel document needed to cross borders.

clue.text: Doctor hands out a large amount

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician giving away a generous sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a large number, used loosely for a great many.

clue.text: Certainly not rare commendation

definitions.meaning: meat cooked thoroughly, the opposite of rare
words of praise for a job

explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked through is the opposite of rare; the phrase is also an exclamation of praise.

clue.text: A wary grey

parts.note: shy means cautious or wary

explanation.surface: A cautious grey animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means pale grey, the colour of ash.

clue.text: Bury it for friendship's sake

parts.note: an idiom about making peace by burying a weapon

explanation.surface: Advice to let a grudge go for the sake of a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury the hatchet, a small axe, is an idiom for ending a quarrel.

clue.text: Station clear of the rink

parts.note: off means away from or clear of
a rink's surface is ice

explanation.surface: A skater ordered to get off the ice to their position.
explanation.definitionFit: Station and office both mean a position or post someone holds.

clue.text: Going up and down the grass

indicators.note: in a down clue reading up or down gives the same letters, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something rising and falling in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes.

clue.text: Article in support of bogus priest

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath, so the article comes last

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backing a fake cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a priest or healer in tribal religions who contacts spirits.

clue.text: Starts the card game and it's shambles!

definitions.meaning: mixing the pack is the first step of any card game
walks with a dragging awkward gait

explanation.definitionFit: Mixing cards before dealing; and dragging the feet when walking, the verb shambles.

clue.text: Left lying in the sand to achromatize

indicators.note: lying in places the letter inside the word for a sandy shore

parts.note: a beach is the sand at the seaside

explanation.surface: Something left out in the sand loses its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach is to remove colour, which is what achromatize means.

clue.text: Whirlpool activity

indicators.note: whirl means spin around, so the letters of the following word are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Something to do in a hot tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whirlpool' looks like one word, but splits into an anagram signal and its fodder; water polo is a pool game.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a sport, a pastime or activity.

clue.text: Plant ten in a soil substitute

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the rearranged letters
a substitute stands in for something, here the letters stand in a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A gardener planting ten specimens in artificial compost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substitute' rearranges A SOIL to OALIS, and 'in' puts X within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxalis is a genus of plants such as wood sorrel.

clue.text: Initial arrangement

parts.note: a design made by interweaving the first letters of a person's names

explanation.definitionFit: A design of interlaced initials embroidered or engraved as a personal mark.

clue.text: Contracted dermatitis using this farm equipment

indicators.note: the answer uses letters spanning the two words, run together

explanation.surface: A farmhand caught a skin rash while operating a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedder is a machine that spreads and turns hay to dry it.

clue.text: Lad grabbing middle-aged chap used to threaten children

indicators.note: grabbing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: middle asks for the central letters of the word aged

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A youth seizing a man in his forties or fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-aged' reads as one adjective, but 'middle' is the selection signal and 'aged' the word it works on; 'grabbing' wraps the lad round that pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is an imaginary monster invoked to frighten children into behaving.
